Ship from stock

Ship a sales order for an item already in stock, and check that inventory went down by the quantity shipped.

Status
Verified
Module
Sales, Warehousing
Length
7 tasks, 60 steps
Updated
25 Oct 2026
Applies to

TaskWhat you doResultSteps

Before you start

  • A customer set up as a sold-to business partner, and an item with stock in a warehouse of your site. To put test stock in a warehouse, follow Purchase order to warehouse receipt.

Procedure

1Confirm there is stock

Result
You know a warehouse whose on-hand, less what is allocated, covers the quantity to ship.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Inventory 360 shows what's on hand, and Allocated shows how much of it other orders have already claimed. Stock is often spread across several warehouses. The sales order has to name one that holds enough, or LN won't find stock to pick. This task is where you choose that warehouse.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Type the item in the filter box above the grid's Item column and press EnterThe item's row, and a row for any item whose code starts with it, showing On Hand · Blocked · On Order · Allocated
1.2Tick the item's own rowThe header links become available
1.3In the Inventory group of the header, click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory (whwmd2515m000) opens with the item already filled in
1.4Read Inventory on Hand and Inventory Allocated per warehouseThe totals are under the gridWrite downitemwarehouseon-handallocated

2Create and approve the sales order

Result
The order status is In Process.
Screen
Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench (tdsls4601m200)

Why LN works this way. Only approved lines can be released to warehousing. If you skip approval, the release may fail later without a clear reason. The Order Acknowledgement that prints shows the sales order number, and the warehousing order uses the same number.

StepActionYou should see
2.1In the header, click New
2.2Enter your customer as Sold-to Business Partner, press TabAddress fills in
2.3Check the Order Type LN fills in, and change it if your order needs anotherExampleOrder Type N10 — Standard orders (no ATP)
2.4Check Planned Delivery Date and Planned Receipt Date, and change them if the customer needs another dayExamplePlanned Delivery Date 2026-10-24 — left at the order datePlanned Receipt Date 2026-10-24 — left at the planned delivery dateBoth start at the Order Date
2.5Check Sales Office and Site on the Order tab
2.6Set Warehouse to the warehouse recorded at step 1.4
2.7Click SaveStatus = FreeWrite downsales order number
2.8In the lines, click New
2.9Search for and select the Item you checked at step 1.4
2.10Enter the Ordered QuantityExampleOrdered Quantity 5Write downordered quantity
2.11Click Save
2.12In the header, Actions➔ApproveStatus = In Process. The Order Acknowledgement prints. For an item that needs documents, a Conformance Reporting sheet prints too
Create and approve the sales order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Status stuck on FreeThe order isn't approved yet. Choose Actions➔Approve
The order can't be approved yetIf Use Confirmation is selected on the order's terms and conditions or on the sold-to business partner, the customer has to confirm the goods first.
On-hand looks high enough, but the order won't fillCheck Allocated: other orders may already have claimed most of the on-hand. See step 1.4

3Release to warehousing

Result
A warehousing order exists with the sales order's number.
Screen
Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench (tdsls4601m200)

Why LN works this way. Releasing passes the approved lines from Sales to Warehousing. LN creates a warehousing order with the sales order's number, and from then on the warehousing procedure decides what happens next, not the sales order. You release from the Actions menu; the Lines ready for panel only counts lines.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Select your order in the Sales Orders grid
3.2Actions➔Release➔Release to Warehousing…The release session opens
3.3Set Upto Release Date on or after the order line's Release Date. LN offers today as Upto Release Date, and calculates each line's Release Date as its planned delivery date minus the outbound lead timeExampleUpto Release Date 2026-10-24 — the date used in this example; LN offers the day you release
3.4Leave the Options tickedPrint Errors · Print Released Lines · Print to predefined Device
3.5Click RELEASEThe Log Report prints
3.6Open the Order Lines tab
3.7Find your order and tick it
3.8References➔StatusSales Order Line Status (tdsls4534s000) opens on Activities 1. Release Sales Orders to Warehousing = Executed
Release to warehousing: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Clicking RELEASE TO WAREHOUSING in Lines ready for does nothingThat panel only counts lines. Use Actions➔Release instead
Your order isn't in the releaseUpto Release Date is earlier than the order line's Release Date, which is the planned delivery date minus the outbound lead time. Set a later date
No warehousing orderThe release didn't run. Check Activities 1 at step 3.8. If it reads Free, run it from Actions➔Release
Activity shows Automatic: NoThat activity doesn't run on its own in this configuration. Run it from Actions➔Release➔Release to Warehousing…

4Generate outbound advice

Result
Advised and Released both show the ordered quantity, and the picking list prints.
Screen
Warehousing➔Manager Dashboard (whinh2300m000)

Why LN works this way. Generating advice is LN choosing which stock, from which locations, fills each outbound line. If the warehousing order type's outbound procedure releases advice automatically, the same action fills Released too and prints the picking list; if not, you release it yourself.

StepActionYou should see
4.1In the order grid at the bottom, filter Order on your sales order numberIts row: Origin Sales, a sales outbound order type such as 20- SO/SC Out, Transaction Type Issue
4.2Tick the row
4.3Click Drill InWarehousing Order (whinh2100m100) opens
4.4Open the Outbound Lines tabLine Status = Open
4.5Tick the outbound line
4.6On the Outbound Lines toolbar, Actions➔Advice➔Generate AdviceThe Picking List by Location prints to its own tab, or the Select Device dialog opens, or nothing opens
4.7If the Select Device dialog opened, click CONTINUEThe Picking List by Location prints to its own tab
4.8If nothing opened, read Advised Quantity and Released Quantity on the outbound lineAdvised Quantity shows the ordered quantity. An empty Released Quantity means the release is still to do
4.9If Released Quantity is empty, choose Actions➔Advice➔Release Advice on the Outbound Lines toolbarThe Picking List by Location prints to its own tab
4.10Read the picking list's headerWrite downRunMission
4.11Go back to the Warehousing Order tabThe outbound line
4.12Read Advised Quantity and Released Quantity on the outbound lineBoth show the ordered quantity
4.13Open the Shipment Lines tabUsually empty. If projected shipments are switched on, a Projected or Open line may already show a Shipment
Generate outbound advice: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Your order isn't in the order gridThe Order filter may be wrong, or the release may not have run. See step 3.8
Advice greyed out on the Actions menuYou're on the session toolbar. The advice actions are on the Outbound Lines toolbar. See step 4.6
Generate Advice greyed out, or Advised Quantity already filled before step 4.6Advice already exists: some configurations generate it on release. To start over, use Undo Advice
The outbound line's status reads PlannedA planned line can't be advised. Choose Activate on the warehousing order, and the line becomes Open.
The order won't adviseCheck that the header Warehouse holds the stock, against step 1.4

5Pick the goods

Result
The outbound line reads Staged, and a shipment line exists.
Screen
Warehousing➔Outbound/Inspections➔Picking List (whinh4525m100)

Why LN works this way. The picking list records stock moving to staging, and confirming it fills Picked. You need this task where the warehouse is location-controlled and its outbound procedure's Picking List activity is manual; otherwise LN fills Picked on release. Once a line is staged, LN creates the shipment line.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Read Run in the headerThe Run from step 4.10
5.2If it is your Run, go on to step 5.4. If it is another Run, click FindPicking List - Search opens
5.3Type your Run in Run and click OKYour Run in the header
5.4Confirm Warehouse and MissionMission is the Mission from step 4.10
5.5Read the grid linesOne line per location the stock comes from: Picked · Sequence · Item · Serial Number · From Location. Picked shows a grey dot
5.6Pick the goods on each line from its From Location to its To Location
5.7Tick the lines you picked
5.8Actions➔Pick RunPicked shows a green tick. On the Warehousing Order, the line status becomes Staged
5.9Go back to the Warehousing Order tabThe order from Generate outbound advice
5.10Open the Shipment Lines tabA shipment line now exists. The shipment number is the first part of Shipment Line, before the line's own number:Write downshipment number
Pick the goods: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No Picking node under WarehousingThere isn't one. Picking is under Outbound/Inspections
Released Quantity is filled but Picked Quantity is emptyThat's expected. They are separate columns, and this task fills Picked
Run empty on the Picking ListAdvice may not have been generated, so nothing was released. Go back to step 4.6

6Ship

Result
The shipment reads Confirmed.
Screen
Warehousing➔Shipments➔Shipments (whinh4130m000)

Why LN works this way. Freezing locks the shipment's contents, and confirming takes the stock out of inventory. The status only changes through those two actions; you can't set it by hand. Where the warehousing order type sets Freeze Mandatory, you freeze before you can confirm. A confirmed shipment can't be changed: to correct it, you need a return shipment.

StepActionYou should see
6.1Filter Shipment on the shipment number from step 5.10Its row
6.2Tick the row
6.3Click Drill InShipment opens. Status = Open. Freeze Mandatory ticked; Allow Changes to Shipment ticked
6.4Read the Shipped Quantity. To ship less than was picked, change it on Shipment Lines (whinh4131m000), not hereExampleShipped Quantity 5 — the ordered quantity, all pickedWrite downshipped quantity
6.5Click FREEZE on the toolbarStatus = Frozen. Allow Changes to Shipment clears and CONFIRM becomes available. The Bill of Lading and the Packing Slip print, each to its own tab
6.6Open the Packing Slips tabThe Packing Slip
6.7Check the customer it ships to, the shipment number, the order and line, the item and the shipped quantity against the orderThey match the order and the quantity you're shipping
6.8Go back to the Shipment tabStatus = Frozen
6.9Click CONFIRM on the toolbarStatus = Confirmed. The stock leaves inventory
Ship: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The shipment won't confirmThe line may not be picked. Check the Picked column on Outbound Lines, then do Pick the goods
The shipment won't confirm, and a validation message showsIf the order type validates shipments, fix any message marked Blocking first. If you reopen a frozen shipment, it's validated again.
The shipment won't confirm, and it has handling unitsIf Handling Unit Based Confirmation is set on a linked line, confirm the handling units first. Whether the line then confirms on its own is an order-type setting, Confirm Shipment Lines when confirming Handling Units. If that's cleared, the line stays Frozen until you confirm it

7Verify it worked

Result
On-hand in that warehouse fell by the quantity shipped, once anything else that moved the item is allowed for.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Check the same item and warehouse you checked in Confirm there is stock. This confirms that inventory changed as expected.

StepActionYou should see
7.1Filter the item in Inventory 360, as at step 1.1The item's row
7.2Tick the item's row
7.3Click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory opens with the item filled in
7.4Read Inventory on Hand for the warehouse you recorded at step 1.4Write downon-hand afterdifference

On-hand before − on-hand after should equal the shipped quantity, in the same unit, as long as nothing else moved the item in that warehouse. On-hand before is the figure from step 1.4. If they differ, check that the shipment reads Confirmed. Then open Item Transactions from Inventory 360 to see what else moved the item. Ship from stock is done when the shipment is Confirmed and the drop in on-hand matches the quantity shipped, after allowing for anything else that moved the item.

Variations

Variations
CaseWhat changes
Standalone advice sessionsWarehousing➔Outbound/Inspections holds Generate Outbound Advice and Release Outbound Advice as their own sessions. Use them for a batch of orders rather than one
Direct ReleaseActions➔Advice➔Direct Release sits beside Generate Advice. This guide doesn't use it: where release is automatic, Generate Advice already releases.
UndoingBefore picking, to start an outbound line over: Undo Advice removes its advice so it can be generated again, and Undo Advice/Release (Shift+Z) takes back the release too and removes the picking list. All are on Actions➔Advice on the Outbound Lines toolbar
Release is manual
Task 4		The warehousing order type's outbound procedure has Release Outbound Advice as a manual activity, so step 4.6 only advises; steps 4.8 and 4.9 release it
Pick Mission / Pick Advice
Task 5		Use these to pick one mission or one advice line instead of the whole run. See step 5.8
Shipping less than ordered
Task 6		Reduce Shipped Quantity on Shipment Lines (whinh4131m000); see step 6.4. Confirming the shipment creates a backorder for the rest, and the backorder becomes a new order line once Sales confirms it.

What comes next

WhenThenStart at
The shipment is Confirmed and inventory has decreasedThis guide ends here. Invoicing is done in Financials, which this guide doesn't cover—
The order could not be filled from stockReplenish first: make it with Production order, move it with Warehouse transfer, or buy it in with Purchase to receipt; then start again at Create and approve the sales orderConfirm there is stock

Known gaps

The library has no source for these yet, so this Document says nothing about them rather than guess.

  • Task 2, if something goes wrong: The order can't be approved yet
  • Task 4, if something goes wrong: The outbound line's status reads Planned
  • Task 6, if something goes wrong: The shipment won't confirm, and a validation message shows
  • Variation: Direct Release
  • Variation: Shipping less than ordered
